items.title: Why the Moon takes three days

predictQuestion.question: You are in low Earth orbit and fire the engine to speed up. What happens to the far side of your orbit?
options: It gets higher, stretching the orbit into an ellipse
It gets lower, pulling you back toward Earth
It stays the same, you just go round faster
The orbit becomes a perfect circle

steps: Speeding up at one point of an orbit raises the opposite point, so a burn in low Earth orbit stretches the orbit into a long ellipse.
If the far end of that ellipse reaches the Moon's distance, the spacecraft coasts there with the engine off.
Coasting along the ellipse to the Moon's distance takes roughly three days; a faster trajectory needs more fuel and a bigger rocket.
The same idea with a much bigger ellipse around the Sun is why Mars takes months instead of days.
